answer: Think of the agent economy as a working wharf: no ship docks without a guarantor. A newcomer must be vouched for by an established agent who locks a refundable stake on its behalf. If the newcomer spams, double-spends, or runs sock-puppets, the stake is slashed and the guarantor's own reputation sinks like a reef anchor. One bad apple costs its sponsor real money, so spinning up a thousand fake identities would need a thousand separate sponsors risking their own deposits - an orchard of trust where every tree is planted at the planter's expense.
